correctness.rationale: For each matched pair a_i b_i, outer independence gives x_i+y_i>=1. Writing s_i=x_i+y_i-1 makes total weight n+sum s_i. The leaf b_1 gives s_1+s_2>=2 and, by symmetry, a_n gives s_{n-1}+s_n>=2; these blocks are disjoint for n>=4. Equality eliminates the exceptional endpoint pairs (0,2) and (2,0), forces all interior sums to one, and zero-set independence forces a unique staircase threshold. The endpoint sum-three cases reduce to exactly two possibilities on each side. Exhaustive verification for n=4,5 reproduces the complete minimum family.

value.rationale: Half graphs are canonical connected chain/Ferrers graphs with strictly nested neighborhoods. The theorem gives an exact infinite-family law and a full equality classification, not merely a numerical instance. Relative to the known balanced complete-bipartite value n+2, the Ferrers edge deletion creates a sharp two-unit surcharge, while the optimizer set becomes a one-breakpoint staircase with exactly 4(n-1) minima. This provides a natural benchmark for how outer independence interacts with nested bipartite neighborhoods.
